evidence.detail: PR #14917 'Support equivalent Universes Within card names' — changed decklist.py so identical canonical names accumulate counts (add_card) instead of raising InvalidDataException; this removes the 'Invalid cards: Glenn' error when both UB and UW names are submitted

normalize() now uses add_card() which sums counts for the same canonical name; old code raised InvalidDataException('More than one entry for {name}') which was caught and produced 'Invalid cards: Glenn'
use_submitted_aliases_in_card_messages() now annotates errors like 'Gregor, Shrewd Magistrate (entered as Glenn, the Voice of Calm; Gregor, Shrewd Magistrate)' — clear explanation of the duplicate

triage.notes: The fix depends on Scryfall storing the Walking Dead card names (Glenn, Negan, etc.) as flavor_names on the Universes Within cards (Gregor, Malik, etc.). The Negan/Malik case is explicitly tested at magic/decklist_test.py:808; Glenn/Gregor follows the same mechanism.
triage.proposed_comment: This was fixed by PR #14917 (commit 2a40b50e). Entering both the Universes Beyond name and the Universes Within name now produces a clear 'too many copies' error that names both the canonical card and the entered aliases, rather than the unhelpful 'Invalid cards' message.

verify.final_comment: Fixed by PR #14917 (commit 2a40b50e). Universes Beyond names are now recognized as valid aliases for their Universes Within equivalents, so entering both names accumulates to 8 copies and produces a clear 'too many copies' error that identifies the canonical card and each submitted alias, replacing the unhelpful 'Invalid cards' message.

own_evidence.detail: normalize() now resolves UB names to canonical via oracle.valid_name(); add_card() accumulates counts, so 4 UB + 4 UW = 8 total, triggering Legality_Too_Many rather than Invalid cards
use_submitted_aliases_in_card_messages() appends '(entered as X)' parenthetical when submitted name differs from canonical, making the error message informative
Explicit test case for two submitted aliases in Legality_Too_Many error matches the exact scenario from the issue
